The plaintiff company being duly registered as Non Banking Financial Institution with Reserve Bank of India deals in business of leasing and financing the vehicles and consumer durable goods along with the other finance facilities/ personal loan to its clients.

3. It is averred that the defendants approached the plaintiff and availed the facility of finance for the purchase of Hero Splendor Plus motorcycle under the Loan Hypothecation Agreement no.DT14151 dated 01.11.2017 for a sum of Rs.42,600/.
Defendant no. 1 was the borrower and defendant no.2 stood guarantor to the aforesaid loan hypothecation agreement.

After due execution of necessary documents, the plaintiff released the aforesaid payment under the said agreement vide consolidated cheque no.014581 dated 23.01.2018 drawn on City Union Bank, in favour of "ARC Motors Pvt. Ltd."
and the defendant received the above said product from the dealer.

sentences.text: The plaint otherwise, as per the amended CPC, besides being verified, is also supported by a affidavit of the plaintiff.

I failed to fathom any reason for according any additional sanctity to the affidavit by way of examination in chief then to the affidavit in support of the plaint or to any exhibit mark being put on the documents which have been filed by the plaintiff and are already on record.
I have therefore, heard the counsel for the plaintiff on merits qua relief of injunction...."

The onus to establish its case rested on plaintiff.

The plaintiff has relied upon original loan Hypothecation Agreement, copy of bank statement, original invoice, account statements maintained by the plaintiff against the account of defendant and legal notice dated 14.11.2019 to prove its case.
8. The suit has been filed on 30.07.2020 which is within the prescribed period of limitation.

It is submitted that Loan Hypothecation Agreement between the plaintiff and defendants was executed at the head office of plaintiff in Delhi, hence, this court has territorial jurisdiction to pass the decree against the defendant.
9. The plaintiff has also claimed delay penalty/ interest at the rate of 5% per moth amounting to Rs.21,422/ and cheque returning charges of Rs.2950/.

As per Section 74 of Indian Contract Act 1872, where, the contract contains stipulation by way of penalty, the party complaining of the breach is entitled to receive from the party who has broken the contract a reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named or the penalty stipulated for.

In the present case, claim of interest @ 5 % per month is certainly excessive and as the name of interest (Delay Penalty) suggests, the same is in the form of Penalty which is not permissible U/s 74 of Indian Contract Act.

10. In the facts and circumstances of the present case, in the opinion of the court, the ends of the justice would be met if the plaintiff is granted prelitigation, pendentelite and future interest @ 18 %

Accordingly, the suit is decreed in favour of plaintiff and against the defendant no.1 and following reliefs are granted to the plaintiff:
1.

A money decree for a sum of Rs.42,185/ (Rupees Forty Two Thousand and One Hundred Eighty Five Only) alongwith with prelitigation, pendentelite and future interest @ 18% per annum from the date of balance due i.e. 10.01.2019 till the date of realization of the amount.

The plaintiff is also entitled for cheque returning charges amounting to Rs.2,500/.
2. Costs of the suit.
